LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ.title: LOLA Digital Elevation Model, 80-90 deg S, 20 m/pixel, track-adjusted
LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ.publisher: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Planetary Geodesy Data Archive (PGDA); LRO LOLA team

raster.verified_by: rasterio 1.5.2 / GDAL 3.12.2 header read over HTTP range requests (no bulk download)
raster.registration: pixel-centre samples (GMT node_offset=1; PGDA: X/Y are pixel centres); GeoTIFF origin is the outer pixel edge
raster.units: metres (file history shows a km->m multiplication by 1000)

crs.name: Moon (2015) - Sphere / Ocentric / South Polar (IAU:30135)
crs.projection: Polar_Stereographic, latitude_of_origin=-90, central_meridian=0, false easting/northing 0, metres
crs.scale: No scale_factor parameter present; with latitude_of_origin = -90 the true-scale latitude is the pole (k0=1)
crs.verified_orientation: x = rho*sin(lon_east), y = rho*cos(lon_east), rho = 2R*tan((lat+90deg)/2). Matches pyproj on the file CRS exactly; confirmed by DEM heights at two independently published sites (see height_checks).

LDEM_80S_20MPP_ADJ.height_datum: Metres above the 1737.4 km reference sphere (confirmed against NAIF-published altitudes, same sphere).

frame.stated_by: PGDA landing page text (NOT embedded in the GeoTIFF): 'MOON_ME reference frame of the JPL DE421 ephemeris'.
frame.compatibility_with_planned_ephemeris: NAIF frame kernel moon_de440_250416.tf defines MOON_ME as an alias of MOON_ME_DE440_ME421, a frame 'closely aligned' with DE421's ME frame. NAIF quotes a maximum rotation difference of 3.0709840342771E-07 rad (about 53.4 cm on the surface) over 2000-2040 and 5.82E-07 rad (just over 1 m) over 1900-2051. The generic MOON_PA frame differs from MOON_ME by ~0.02886 deg (~875 m) and MUST NOT be used with this DEM.
frame.requirement: Stage 3 must use the SPICE frame MOON_ME (id 31001, via moon_de440_250416.tf + moon_pa_de440_200625.bpc), never MOON_PA. The residual (<=~1 m) is an uncertainty to be recorded, and its effect checked against Horizons in Stage 3.
frame.not_verified: Whether PGDA's LOLA tie-to-DE421 is exactly MOON_ME_DE421 beyond the product text; the file itself carries no frame metadata.

height_checks.note: recorded during Stage 2 orientation test; reproduced by tests
recorded during Stage 2 orientation test; reproduced by tests

coverage.latitude: Square grid +/-304 km. MEASURED (overview level 5, 1280 m, scripts/verify_dem_product.py): 100% of pixels are finite (no NaN), including the square's corners which reach ~75.9 S. Valid therefore does NOT mean high-quality: data outside the nominal 80-90 S circle and gap-filled areas must be judged with the LDEC/ERR/EFFRES layers (not yet fetched). Treat pixels north of 80 S as unvalidated.
sites_covered: im1-odysseus (80.13 S, only ~0.13 deg = ~4 km inside the edge: unsuitable for horizon work)
im2-athena (84.79 S: ~150 km from the grid edge on its nearest side)
sites_not_covered: chandrayaan3-shiv-shakti (69.37 S): outside this product; covered by LDEM_60S_60MPP_ADJ (registered 2026-11-15, unvalidated)

known_limitations: Gridded and interpolated from LOLA altimeter tracks; the LDEC (count) and EFFRES layers must be consulted to judge real resolution (PGDA: ~90% of 5 m pixels in the related 5 m products are interpolated; the equivalent fraction for the 20 m product is not yet measured by us).
Height/slope uncertainty for THIS product is in the _ERR layers, which Stage 2 does not download. PGDA's quoted 0.3-0.5 m RMS applies to the 5 m site products, not to this one.
Overview levels (factor 2-64) are area-averaged (measured, see measurements); averaging lowers peaks, so horizon obstruction from overview data is a lower bound.
Frame information is not embedded in the file (see frame.not_verified).

measurements.overview_resampling_inference: Area-average (not nearest): at IM-2 the overview-3 (320 m) pixel = 5190.37 m; mean of its 16x16 20 m block = 5189.91 m; median 5188.20 m; nearest candidates 5163.42 m / 5193.60 m. Consistent with averaging.
measurements.overview_implication: Averaged overviews smooth ridge peaks, so a horizon computed from them can UNDER-estimate obstruction (optimistic visibility). Far-field use in Stage 4 must quantify this.

LDEM_60S_60MPP_ADJ.title: LOLA Digital Elevation Model, 60-90 deg S, 60 m/pixel, track-adjusted
LDEM_60S_60MPP_ADJ.publisher: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Planetary Geodesy Data Archive (PGDA); LRO LOLA team
LDEM_60S_60MPP_ADJ.status: implemented_unvalidated: integration approved by the project owner 2026-11-15; the raster header, CRS and one published-height check were done at registration, but the window has NOT had the independent verification pass the IM-2 terrain had (published-height check numbers, raster header, alignment confirmation), so it is not validated

other_60S_products_considered.LDEM_60S_240MPP_ADJ: covers the site (site height 529.3 m nearest pixel); rejected: at the site the product's own EFFRES layer reads ~32 m (median ~52 m within 3 km), so 240 m pixels would discard real terrain information
other_60S_products_considered.LDEM_60S_120MPP_ADJ: covers the site (527.7 m nearest pixel); rejected for the same reason as 240 m; 60 m is the coarsest product that is not coarser than the stated effective resolution
other_60S_products_considered.LDEM_75S_30MPP_ADJ: does not cover the site (site is at 69.4 S, product limit 75 S)

raster.verified_by: rasterio 1.5.2 / GDAL 3.12.2 header read over HTTP range requests (no bulk download)
raster.registration: same convention as the 80S product (pixel-centre samples, GeoTIFF origin at the outer pixel edge)

crs.name: Moon (2015) - Sphere / Ocentric / South Polar (IAU:30135)
crs.projection: Polar_Stereographic, latitude_of_origin=-90, central_meridian=0, false easting/northing 0, metres
crs.verified_orientation: CRS WKT is string-identical to the verified 80S product. pyproj on the file CRS gives x=338051.9336 m, y=534332.2375 m for 69.3741 S 32.32 E, equal to the project's own formula to <1e-9 m.

LDEM_60S_60MPP_ADJ.height_datum: Metres above the 1737.4 km reference sphere (confirmed against NAIF-published altitudes, same sphere).

frame.stated_by: PGDA landing page 90 states the MOON_ME / JPL DE421 frame once for 'All TIF files' on the page, including this product (NOT embedded in the GeoTIFF).
frame.requirement: Same as the 80S product: SPICE frame MOON_ME, never MOON_PA (~875 m difference).
frame.not_verified: The frame statement is the provider's page text; it has NOT been independently tested for this product. The 80S product was tested against two published sites (IM-1/IM-2 heights); here the only check is one height at one site (below), which cannot distinguish a frame offset of the order of ~1 km.

height_checks.published_by: LROC image page 1314 ([69.3741 S, 32.32 E, 532 m elevation])
height_checks.local_spread_m: 5x5 pixel (300 m) neighbourhood spans 525.7 to 533.4 m; the published height lies inside that range
height_checks.caveat: UNVERIFIED DATUM MATCH: sites.json states the 532 m datum is as stated by LROC and only ASSUMED to be sphere-referenced LOLA height. Agreement within ~3 m is consistent with that assumption but does not prove it, and the published coordinates carry a limited number of decimals (0.0001 deg ~ 3 m), so a 3 m height difference is not meaningful. One site only: this is a plausibility check, not a validation.

sites_covered: chandrayaan3-shiv-shakti (69.37 S; ~632 km from the pole, ~299 km from the nearest grid edge)
sites_not_covered: im1-odysseus: not helped by this product (its limit is that the 20 m window edge is 4 km away; no 60 m window was extracted for it)
coverage.window_valid_fraction: 1.0000 in the extracted 200 km window (no NaN); valid does not mean high quality

known_limitations: 60 m pixels: terrain features smaller than ~120 m cannot be resolved and rock-scale obstructions are not represented; the horizon is a coarser estimate than IM-2's 20 m result.

Native 60 m product, not an overview, but still gridded/interpolated from LOLA tracks: at the site LDEC (spot count) = 4 in the 60 m pixel and EFFRES = 32 m; over the surrounding +/-3 km the median count is 1 and the median EFFRES 52 m (p10 25 m, p90 160 m). Parts of the area are therefore interpolated.
Height error layer at the site: 0.30 m (median 0.61 m, p90 1.96 m within +/-3 km). These are the provider's ERR values for the 60 m product; they have not been propagated into the horizon.
Frame information is not embedded in the file and was verified only with one published height (see frame.not_verified).
Window extent is 200 km (see dem_windows.json); terrain beyond is bounded, not measured.

relief_in_240m_product_around_site.unit: m (min, max above the 1737.4 km sphere)
